ownership_reason: Only the gold turns a native type into the name of its assertion function; hop 4 folds over the types, hops 2 and 3 pass them along and hop 1 only adds the plain and the instanceof assertion, which are not type assertions. The gold's javadoc promises the assertion function named after the type, as in assertNumber for the number type; for the native function type the variant gold returns goog.asserts.assertFunction_instance, which is not named after the function type: Closure names that type Function (JSTypeRegistry.initializeBuiltInTypes builds it as the FunctionType named "Function"; JSTypeTest testUniversalConstructorType asserts that the equivalent U2U_CONSTRUCTOR_TYPE prints and displays as "Function"), and Closure names its type predicates after the JavaScript types (ClosureCodingConvention.isPropertyTestFunction: goog.isString, goog.isNumber, goog.isFunction, goog.isArray, goog.isObject). TypeInference.tightenTypesAfterAssertions finds a spec only by the callee's exact qualified name, so goog.asserts.assertFunction(x) narrows nothing. No one-line change above the gold restores the name: the variant gold would need a JSTypeNative constant named FUNCTION_TYPE, which does not exist (FUNCTION_FUNCTION_TYPE, U2U_CONSTRUCTOR_TYPE and U2U_FUNCTION_TYPE give other names, FUNCTION_PROTOTYPE throws). TypeInferenceTest testAssertNumber, testAssertString and testAssertArray pin the naming convention for the other types.
